paper.name: The House of 1400
paper.motto: An afternoon newspaper for one reader

big_days.rule: The signed editor's note runs only on a big day for Parth, judged by his relevance, not by sport alone. Name the kind in edition big_day.

kinds.club_match: An important match for the followed football club (follows.football_club): a final, a knockout tie, a Clasico, a title or relegation decider, a top-of-the-table clash.
kinds.cricket_match: An important match for the followed cricket team (follows.cricket_team): a final, semi-final or quarter-final, a series decider, India v Pakistan, a World Cup or Champions Trophy game.
kinds.f1_decider: A race weekend where the followed driver (follows.f1_driver) can win or lose the title, or a season opener or finale.
kinds.tennis_final: A followed tennis player (follows.tennis_players) in a Grand Slam semi-final or final.
kinds.money_day: A day that moves his money or prices: Union Budget, an RBI rate decision, a market crash or record, a tax or rule change taking effect.
kinds.national_moment: National election results, a story that leads every national front page, or a major event in Bengaluru, Ranchi or Prayagraj.
kinds.work_day: Big news for his work: US wholesale or retail, B2B SaaS, or the AI tools he uses.
kinds.paper_day: The paper's own milestones: launch, the 100th edition, a new section.

paper.reader: Parth. SDR manager at a B2B SaaS company selling to US wholesale and retail. Works 17:00 to 02:00 IST on weekdays. Reads mostly on a Nothing Phone 3 in Chrome, sometimes on a MacBook.

desks_v2.note: The new design (behind ?v2 until Parth switches it on, 1 Oct 2026): Page One, then six desks, each its own page behind one row of tabs. A section no desk names is not shown in v2. Your Desk prints folded at the foot of Off Duty.

knockouts.note: Any cup Madrid are in a knockout round of is drawn in The Wider Pitch, found from Madrid's own ESPN schedule across all competitions (Parth, 1 Oct: not a fixed list). Leagues and friendlies are not cups.

rival_club_line.name: Barcelona
rival_club_line.rule: one dry line only for a real loss, knockout, setback or funny incident

primary: India and world news (must-know floor), including India's institutions (elections, courts, Parliament, regulators, constitutional offices) when they lead the national news; see EDITORIAL.md

India money: rules, proposals, charges, taxes and rates that change what people in India pay, earn, save, borrow, invest or insure; and the causes of big moves in Indian stocks and sectors (EDITORIAL.md, money test)
Entertainment: English and Hindi films and series, theatre and OTT
Your Desk from Calendar and Gmail
secondary: India credit cards: any change, not only points
AI tools and automation for work
rules: No player-milestone chasing (e.g. career goal counts)
No Curry-specific coverage beyond major news
No gossip, weak rumours or routine previews

Sensex: to be found; skip until two sources exist

movers.universe: Nifty 500 (NSE's published constituent list, fetched live)
movers.rule: Every flagged move is a question the daily run must answer: find why it moved. If the cause is a rule, a regulator, a policy, a result or a deal that matters beyond one ticker, it is a Ledger story (Front Page when it hits a household name or everyone's money). Record the answer in checks.movers.

mood.method: Published readings, never our own calculation. India: Tickertape's Market Mood Index, from foreign investors' flows, volatility (India VIX), momentum, market breadth, price strength and demand for gold, updated through the trading day. US: CNN's Fear & Greed Index, from seven readings (stock momentum and strength, breadth, put and call options, junk-bond demand, volatility and safe-haven demand), updated through the US trading day. Each gauge uses its publisher's own bands and words. If a publisher cannot be reached, the gauge keeps its last reading with that reading's time.

markets.returns_note: 7D and 1M are Moneycontrol's published figures where it publishes them (its Indian figures agree with NSE's own). Where no reliable source publishes them (Nasdaq-100, Brent, the rupee, gold and Bitcoin today), they are worked out from official daily closes and marked as calculated.

weather.family_note: Shown every day: where the reader's parents live. Temperature, humidity, air and the week ahead.

trends.extra_geos_rule: add the F1 host, Madrid opponent, India cricket opponent, ATP host country when relevant

exclude: US economic policy including the Fed
crypto price ladders and daily up/down
betting.override: include an excluded market only if it clearly affects Parth

carry.rule: A market printed in the previous edition carries over while it is open, undecided (favourite under 99%), and still trending: inside the top max_rank markets by 24-hour volume after the exclusions, or its favourite moved min_move_pts points or more since it was printed. A market that ends or is decided hands over to the next market in the same line (next month's edition of the same question). At most max carries, busiest first, so new markets always have room. Nothing is carried because it is named anywhere.

signals.rule: One line in Paddock Notes, Madridismo, The Crease and Deuce with what Polymarket says about the next race or match the paper follows. Found from the live fixtures, never named in code. Markets under min_volume dollars traded are left out.

page_one.note: The market expects, on Page One (Parth, 1 Oct: "How is Brazil important?"): the three busiest markets that touch what he follows. A market naming a follow (config follows: the club, the driver, the players, India and its named players, the NBA team) ranks first; then a season-long market in these categories, or a match of a followed national side; then a war or trade fight that moves markets. A single match of anyone else, other countries' politics and awards never reach Page One; the Betting Window still prints them.

mon.line: Monday edition · the week ahead, and what the weekend did to markets

fri.line: Friday edition · Screen & Stage and Namma Beat run longer today

sun.line: Sunday edition · the week's releases get their verdicts

upcoming.note: TMDB windows for Screen & Stage candidates: films and series due in the next days_ahead days, and cinema releases of the last days_back days now streaming in India; per_language most popular in Hindi and in English.

site.telegram_ping: lead headline + link, only after the edition is verified live

sources.note: The daily reading list (the Wire), read by /api/live/wire. During the source trial (see `trial`) the daily run does not use it while making the paper; scripts/trial.mjs reads it only after the edition is live. kind: signal = Google News top and topic pages (their order and related-coverage lists rank and group the day), search = Google News search (discovery only, never cited), official = a regulator or body, news = an outlet. Stories never cite the Wire: they cite the publisher's own page. Tested 28 Sep 2026.

feeds.name: The Times of India, top stories
Golden State of Mind (SB Nation, Warriors)
Axios, technology and AI business (via Google News)

tiers.note: Tier 1: official and primary sources. Tier 2: reputable outlets. Anything else is tier 3. Scored in the trial only, until Parth switches it on (then a validator warning, never a failure).

paywalled.note: Parth has no subscription to these (1 Oct 2026). Their feeds (NYT Technology, Science, Well; The Athletic's football, Real Madrid, F1, tennis and Warriors) are leads (kind: lead): the wire finds where else each story is reported, and the paper reads and links an open outlet. A story whose only sources are these hosts fails validation.

not_outlets.note: Social networks and aggregators that Google News lists beside real outlets: never a source for the paper.

top_check.note: The desk check (from 2 Oct 2026, Parth, after the Ronaldo and Ocon misses): every feed's top stories in the window are read and answered by the editor, grouped by event whatever the wording. Titles matching skip are routine notices, never news. A feed's own top (Back Home's local searches: 3) replaces per_feed for that feed.

trial.note: Source trial (from 28 Sep), stopped early by Parth on 1 Oct to save run time and tokens: three editions scored, 29 Sep to 1 Oct (ledger/trial/, the /trial page). The daily run no longer runs scripts/trial.mjs. The parts already switched on stay on: Screen & Stage from /api/live/screen, the wire check from /api/live/wire, tennis from ESPN.

illustrator.name: Bunty Brushwala
illustrator.about: The paper's illustrator (the drawings are made by Codex). Bhide orders; Bunty decides what to draw and how.

art.note: Context for Bunty Brushwala, the illustrator, published in /art/brief.json. Inspiration, not rules: Bunty decides the idea and the style. Parth sets any design rules with Bunty directly.
art.paper: The House of 1400: a calm, factual afternoon newspaper for one reader in Bengaluru, edited by the fictional T. A. Bhide, a strict, well-read, dryly witty editor of the old school. Warm newsprint paper, near-black ink, one colour per section.
styles_the_editor_likes: Pen and ink on newsprint, with one accent colour from the story's section
Bold flat colour, modern editorial illustration

selection.note: How the paper chooses what Bunty draws (Parth, 1 Oct 2026). Bhide scores every printed story in the edition's hidden art_scores; scripts/publish.mjs picks the orders from the scores with these settings and writes art_orders, most important first. The brief Bunty reads (/art/brief.json) is unchanged. Nothing here ever stops the paper from printing.

money.note: The India money sweep's sources (EDITORIAL.md, Research). Both groups are read every run and the validator checks that checks.money_sweep has at least one page from each. When a miss shows a body was needed, add it here and record the miss in ledger/lessons.json.

section_ranges.note: The usual upper end of each section (EDITORIAL.md, Section briefs). Going past it is a warning, never an error: keep the strongest and move the rest to briefs, or keep it long if the news is that big. The floors are unchanged (validate.mjs).

watch_in_india.note: Where to watch in India, printed beside a match (Parth, 1 Oct). Fixed rules first; India's cricket from WhereIsCricket (live); tennis only when the run finds two independent Indian sources naming the same streamer (EDITORIAL.md) and writes it into the fixture's `where`. Never Tennis TV.

multi_events.note: Multi-sport and multi-nation events where every India men's (or mixed) knockout match from the quarter-final on, bronze-medal matches included, and every India women's final, in any sport goes into The Fixture List and its result into The Sidelines (Parth, 1 Oct, after the men's hockey semi-final v Pakistan was missed). While an event runs, the edition records India's knockouts in checks.india_knockouts. Add each event here with its dates.
